This report aims at informing on the 2022 status of ambient air quality in Europe and on progress towards meeting the air quality standards established for the protection of health in the Ambient Air Quality Directives (EU, 2004, 2008) (Table 1) and the World Health Organization air quality guideline levels (WHO, 2000, 2006, 2021) (Table 2)(<sup>4</sup>).

Intent of the Sediment Quality Provisions of the Water Quality Control Plan for Enclosed Bays and Estuaries of California It is the goal of the State Water Resources Control Board (State Water Board) to comply with the legislative directive in Water Code section 13393 to adopt sediment quality objectives (SQOs). The Sediment Quality Provisions integrates chemical and biological measures to determine if the sediment-dependent biota are protected or degraded as a result of exposure to toxic pollutants\* in sediment in order to protect benthic\* communities in enclosed bays\* and estuaries\*, human health, wildlife, and resident finfish. The Sediment Quality Provisions are not intended to address low dissolved oxygen, pathogens or nutrients including ammonia. The State Water Board will continue to refine benthic community protection indicators for estuarine waters and improve the approach to address sediment quality related human health risk associated with consumption of fish tissue. ## 2. Implementation Provisions for SWQPAs-GP\* (a) Implementation provisions for existing point source wastewater discharges (NPDES) (1) An SWQPA-GP shall not be designated over existing permitted point source wastewater outfalls or encroach upon the zone of initial dilution\* associated with an existing discharge. This requirement does not apply to discharges less than one million gallons per day. (2) Designation of an SWQPA-GP shall not include conditions to move existing point source wastewater outfalls. (3) Where a new SWQPA-GP is established in the vicinity of existing municipal wastewater outfalls, there shall be no new or modified limiting condition or prohibitions for the SWQPA-GP relative to those wastewater outfalls. (4) Regulatory requirements for discharges from existing treated municipal wastewater outfalls shall be derived from the Chapter II – Water Quality Objectives and Chapter III – Program of Implementation. (b) Implementation provisions for existing seawater\* intakes (1) Existing permitted seawater\* intakes other than those serving desalination facilities\* must be controlled to minimize entrainment and impingement by using best technology available. Existing permitted seawater\* intakes with a capacity less than one million gallons per day are excluded from this requirement. (2) Existing permitted seawater\* intakes serving desalination facilities are governed by the provisions set forth in chapter III.M of this Plan. (c) Implementation provisions for permitted separate storm sewer system (MS4) discharges and nonpoint source discharges. (1) Existing waste\* discharges are allowed, but shall not cause an undesirable alteration in natural water quality. For purposes of SWQPA-GP, an undesirable alteration in natural water quality means that for intermittent (e.g. wet weather) discharges, Table 1 instantaneous maximum concentrations for chemical constituents, and daily maximum concentrations for chronic toxicity,\* must not be exceeded in the receiving water.\* (2) An NPDES permitting authority\* may authorize NPDES-permitted non-storm water discharges\* to an MS4 with a direct discharge to an SWQPA-GP only to the extent the NPDES permitting authority\* finds that the discharge does not cause an undesirable alteration in natural water quality in an SWQPA-GP. (3) Non-storm water (dry weather) flows are effectively prohibited as required by the applicable permit. Where capacity and infrastructure exists, all dry weather flows shall be diverted to municipal sanitary sewer systems. The permitting authority\* may allow discharges essential for emergency response purposes, structural stability, and slope stability, which may include but are not limited the following: See Appendix I for definition of terms. 2015 Ocean Plan a. Discharges associated with emergency fire-fighting operations. b. Foundation and footing drains c. Water from crawl space or basement pumps. d. Hillside dewatering. (4) The following naturally occurring discharges are allowed: a. Naturally occurring groundwater seepage via a storm drain b. Non-anthropogenic flows from a naturally occurring stream via a culvert or storm drain, as long as there are no contributions of anthropogenic runoff. (5) Existing storm water discharges into an SWQPA-GP shall be characterized and assessed to determine what effect if any these inputs are having on natural water quality in the State Water Quality Protection Area. Such assessments shall include an evaluation of cumulative impacts as well as impacts stemming from individual discharges. Information to be considered shall include: a. Water quality; b. Flow; c. Watershed pollutant sources; and d. Intertidal and/ or subtidal biological surveys. 在环境空气质量方面，GB 3095-2012《环境空气质量标准》表1为环境空气基本污染物项目浓度限值表，涵盖二氧化硫、二氧化氮、一氧化碳、臭氧及粒径小于等于10μm和2.5μm的颗粒物等项目，基本项目在全国范围内实施；GB 3095-2026表1列出上述项目的过渡阶段及一级、二级浓度限值。另有表1规定采样点数量最多可减少50%时各污染物最低采样点数量，按区域人口分档，涵盖二氧化氮、二氧化硫、一氧化碳、苯、PM10、PM2.5、PM10中的铅、镉、砷、镍及苯并(a)芘，最低数量从1个到5个不等。欧盟附件VII第1节的表1规定设于城市背景位置的监测超级站点须测量的污染物及测量类型，包括PM10、PM2.5、UFP、BC、NO2、O3、SO2、CO、超细颗粒物粒径分布、苯并(a)芘及其他多环芳烃及其总沉降、砷镉铅镍及其总沉降、苯和PM2.5化学组成。2022年欧洲空气质量状况报告的表1汇总环境空气质量指令为保护健康确立的空气质量标准，其中O3的信息和警报阈值及NO2、SO2的警报阈值未在该报告中分析。

在水质与室内空气方面，GB 5084-2021《农田灌溉水质标准》表1为农田灌溉用水基本控制项目限值表，按水田作物、旱地作物和蔬菜三类分别给出pH、水温、悬浮物、五日生化需氧量、化学需氧量、阴离子表面活性剂、氯化物、硫化物、全盐量、总铅、总镉、铬、总汞、总砷、粪大肠菌群数和蛔虫卵数等限值。GB 18466-2005表1为传染病和结核病医疗机构污水污染物排放标准值表，共26项控制项目，包括粪大肠菌群数、肠道致病菌、肠道病毒、结核杆菌、pH、COD、BOD、SS、氨氮、总余氯、斑马鱼卵急性毒性及总镉、总铬、六价铬、总砷、总铅、总银、总α放射性、总β放射性等；修改单对其第23至25项及表注内容进行修改，并增加第26项控制项目及标准值；其第16～22项在科室处理设施排出口取样。《室内空气质量标准》表1按物理性、化学性、生物性、放射性四个参数类别列出19项参数的序号、单位、标准值及备注，并注明新风量要求不低于标准值，除温度和相对湿度外的其它参数要求不高于标准值。此外，表1还包含为保护市政与工业有益用途而设的水质目标，地表水环境质量标准基本项目标准限值表亦以表1形式呈现。另有表1规定现有制浆造纸企业水污染物排放限值，包含pH值、色度、悬浮物、BOD5、CODCr、氨氮、总氮、总磷、AOX等指标及单位产品基准排水量。还有表1列出受沉积物质量条款保护的有益用途及其对应目标受体，另有表1为规划清单表格，列出在至少80%置信水平下将水体列入规划清单所需的不满足适用水质基准的最低样本数量。此外，存在用于水质变化趋势分析对照的规定表格。另有表1为按有益用途和水体类型列出“C”值（如12 ng/L、4 ng/L、1 ng/L总汞或逐案确定）的数据表，用于确定排放者的合理潜能和排放限值。

在排放方面，锅炉大气污染物排放标准表1按燃煤锅炉、以油为燃料的锅炉或燃气轮机组、以气体为燃料的锅炉或燃气轮机组等类型分别规定污染物项目、适用条件、限值及污染物排放监控位置。GB 28662-2012表1规定现有企业自2012年10月1日至2014年12月31日执行的大气污染物排放限值。在用锅炉相关标准表1规定在用锅炉自2015年10月1日或2016年7月1日起执行的排放限值，按燃煤、燃油、燃气锅炉分别给出颗粒物、二氧化硫、氮氧化物、汞及其化合物和烟气黑度限值。机动车排放标准表1汇总中国现行新生产机动车排放标准，按车辆类型分列标准标号和标准名称，反映截至2020年12月31日的现行标准情况。此外，Table 1还列出化学物质瞬时最大浓度和慢性毒性日最大浓度限值。

在环境影响评价方面，相关标准表1规定建设项目和规划项目SO2、NOx及VOCs的年排放量门槛：建设项目SO2+NOx≥500 t/a对应二次PM2.5；规划项目SO2+NOx≥500 t/a对应二次PM2.5，NOx+VOCs≥2000 t/a对应O3；当污染物年排放量达到表1规定的量时，可按表4推荐的方法预测二次污染物。此外，“表1”亦见于气象数据文献，指展示2024年珠江区降水量与上年和多年平均值比较情况的数据表；2024年水资源一级区降水量统计表也以“表1”形式呈现，包含各一级区降水量及与多年平均值、2023年的比较。另有表1为包含测试物种及相关参数的表格，用于选择测试物种，涉及测试方法选择时的盐度和层级分类。此外，还存在一种断面水质类别与水质定性评价分级对应关系表，以“表1”形式列出水质类别、水质状况、表征颜色和水质功能。含氯消毒剂设计相关表格中，采用含氯消毒剂时按表1、表2要求设计。

根据提供的上下文，“表1”这个编号在不同标准与文献中指向内容各异的表格，因此无法给出一个统一的“表1”项目与限值清单。以下按来源分别列出：

## 一、GB 3095-2012《环境空气质量标准》表1（环境空气污染物基本项目浓度限值）

- **二氧化硫（SO₂）**：年平均、24小时平均、1小时平均均设一级与二级浓度限值。
- **二氧化氮（NO₂）**：年平均、24小时平均、1小时平均均设一级与二级浓度限值。
- **一氧化碳（CO）**：24小时平均、1小时平均的一级与二级浓度限值，单位为mg/m³。
- **臭氧（O₃）**：日最大8小时平均、1小时平均的一级与二级浓度限值。
- **颗粒物（PM10，粒径≤10μm）**：设一级与二级浓度限值。
- **颗粒物（PM2.5，粒径≤2.5μm）**：设一级与二级浓度限值。

一类区适用一级浓度限值，二类区适用二级浓度限值；基本项目在全国范围内实施。GB 3095-2026表1另列出上述项目的过渡阶段浓度限值（自标准实施之日起至2030年12月31日执行）及一级、二级浓度限值。

## 二、《室内空气质量标准》表1

按物理性、化学性、生物性、放射性四类共19项参数列出序号、单位、标准值及备注。其中化学性类别包括二氧化硫、二氧化氮、一氧化碳、二氧化碳、氨、臭氧、甲醛、苯、甲苯、二甲苯、苯并[a]芘、可吸入颗粒物和总挥发性有机物13项。表中给出的部分标准值为：

- 二氧化硫 0.50 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 二氧化氮 0.24 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 一氧化碳 10 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 二氧化碳 0.10%（日平均值）
- 氨 0.20 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 臭氧 0.16 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 甲醛 0.10 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 苯 0.11 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 甲苯 0.20 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 二甲苯 0.20 mg/m³（1小时均值）
- 苯并[a]芘 1.0 ng/m³（日平均值）
- 温度：夏季空调22~28°C，冬季采暖16~24°C
- 相对湿度：夏季空调40~80%，冬季采暖30~60%
- 氡（²²²Rn）400 Bq/m³（年平均值，属行动水平）

新风量要求不低于标准值；除温度和相对湿度外的其它参数要求不高于标准值。

## 三、GB 5084-2021《农田灌溉水质标准》表1（基本控制项目限值）

按水田作物、旱地作物和蔬菜三类分别给出限值：

- pH：5.5~8.5；水温：不高于35°C
- 悬浮物：水田80 mg/L，旱地100 mg/L，蔬菜按注a为60 mg/L、按注b为15 mg/L
- 五日生化需氧量（BOD₅）：水田60 mg/L，旱地100 mg/L，蔬菜按注a为40 mg/L、按注b为15 mg/L
- 化学需氧量（CODCr）：水田150 mg/L，旱地200 mg/L，蔬菜按注a为100 mg/L、按注b为60 mg/L
- 阴离子表面活性剂：水田5 mg/L，蔬菜5 mg/L，旱地8 mg/L
- 氯化物（以Cl⁻计）：350 mg/L，适用三类作物
- 硫化物（以S²⁻计）：1 mg/L，适用三类作物
- 全盐量：非盐碱土地区1000 mg/L，盐碱土地区2000 mg/L
- 总铅：0.2 mg/L；总镉：0.01 mg/L；铬（六价）：0.1 mg/L；总汞：0.001 mg/L
- 总砷：水田0.05 mg/L，蔬菜0.05 mg/L，旱地0.1 mg/L
- 粪大肠菌群数：水田和旱地均为40000 MPN/L，蔬菜按注a为20000 MPN/L、按注b为10000 MPN/L
- 蛔虫卵数：亦在该表中列出

基本控制项目为必测项目，其各项限值应符合表1的规定。

## 四、GB 18466-2005《医疗机构水污染物排放标准》表1（传染病和结核病医疗机构污水排放标准值，共26项）

- 粪大肠菌群数 100 MPN/L
- 肠道致病菌 不得检出
- 肠道病毒 不得检出
- 结核杆菌 不得检出
- pH 6~9
- 化学需氧量（COD）60 mg/L，最高允许排放负荷60 g/(床位·d)
- 生化需氧量（BOD）20 mg/L，最高允许排放负荷20 g/(床位·d)
- 悬浮物（SS）20 mg/L，最高允许排放负荷20 g/(床位·d)
- 氨氮 15 mg/L
- 动植物油 5 mg/L
- 石油类 5 mg/L
- 阴离子表面活性剂 5 mg/L
- 色度 30（稀释倍数）
- 挥发酚 0.5 mg/L
- 总氰化物 0.5 mg/L
- 总汞 0.05 mg/L
- 总镉 0.1 mg/L
- 总铬 1.5 mg/L
- 六价铬 0.5 mg/L
- 总砷 0.5 mg/L
- 总铅 1.0 mg/L
- 总银 0.5 mg/L
- 总α放射性 1 Bq/L
- 总β放射性 10 Bq/L
- 总余氯（总氯）：总排口（排入水体的要求）0.5 mg/L；接触池出口6.5~10 mg/L且消毒接触池接触时间≥1.5h（仅适用于含氯消毒剂工艺）
- 斑马鱼卵急性毒性（稀释倍数，排入水体的要求）6

传染病和结核病医疗机构污水排放一律执行表1的规定；传染病区污水在进入污水处理系统前应分流并预消毒，并满足表1中粪大肠菌群数、总余氯等限值要求。修改单对表1第23~25项及表注内容进行修改，并增加第26项控制项目及标准值。

## 五、在用锅炉大气污染物排放标准表1

- 颗粒物：燃煤80 mg/m³，燃油60 mg/m³，燃气30 mg/m³
- 二氧化硫：燃煤400 mg/m³，燃油300 mg/m³，燃气100 mg/m³；位于广西壮族自治区、重庆市、四川省和贵州省的燃煤锅炉执行550 mg/m³限值
- 氮氧化物：燃煤、燃油、燃气均为400 mg/m³
- 汞及其化合物：燃煤锅炉0.05 mg/m³，燃油和燃气锅炉不作规定
- 烟气黑度（林格曼黑度）：不大于1级
- 监控位置：烟囱或烟道（烟气黑度监控位置为烟囱排放口）

## 六、现有制浆造纸企业水污染物排放限值表1

包含pH值、色度、悬浮物、BOD₅、CODCr、氨氮、总氮、总磷、AOX等指标及单位产品基准排水量。

## 七、加州《海洋计划》表1（“C”值，按有益用途和水体类型）

用于确定排放者的合理潜能和排放限值：

## 5. Implementation Provisions for SWQPAs-GP\* (a) Implementation provisions for existing point source wastewater discharges (NPDES) (1) An SWQPA-GP shall not be designated over existing permitted point source wastewater outfalls or encroach upon the zone of initial dilution\* associated with an existing discharge. This requirement does not apply to discharges less than one million gallons per day. (2) Designation of an SWQPA-GP shall not include conditions to move existing point source wastewater outfalls. (3) Where a new SWQPA-GP is established in the vicinity of existing municipal wastewater outfalls, there shall be no new or modified limiting condition or prohibitions for the SWQPA-GP relative to those wastewater outfalls. (4) Regulatory requirements for discharges from existing treated municipal wastewater outfalls shall be derived from the Chapter II – Water Quality Objectives and Chapter III – Program of Implementation. (b) Implementation provisions for existing seawater\* intakes (1) Existing permitted seawater\* intakes other than those serving desalination facilities\* must be controlled to minimize entrainment and impingement by using best technology available. Existing permitted seawater\* intakes with a capacity less than one million gallons per day are excluded from this requirement. (2) Existing permitted seawater\* intakes serving desalination facilities are governed by the provisions set forth in chapter III.M of this Plan. (c) Implementation provisions for permitted separate storm sewer system (MS4) discharges and nonpoint source discharges. (1) Existing waste\* discharges are allowed, but shall not cause an undesirable alteration in natural water quality. For purposes of SWQPA-GP, an undesirable alteration in natural water quality means that for intermittent (e.g. wet weather) discharges, Table 1 instantaneous maximum concentrations for chemical constituents, and daily maximum concentrations for chronic toxicity,\* must not be exceeded in the receiving water.\* (2) An NPDES permitting authority\* may authorize NPDES-permitted non-storm water discharges\* to an MS4 with a direct discharge to an SWQPA-GP only to the extent the NPDES permitting authority\* finds that the discharge does not cause an undesirable alteration in natural water quality in an SWQPA-GP. (3) Non-storm water (dry weather) flows are effectively prohibited as required by the applicable permit. Where capacity and infrastructure exists, all dry weather flows shall be diverted to municipal sanitary sewer systems. The permitting authority\* may allow discharges essential for emergency response purposes, structural stability, and slope stability, which may include but are not limited the following: See Appendix I for definition of terms. 2015 Ocean Plan a. Discharges associated with emergency fire-fighting operations. b. Foundation and footing drains c. Water from crawl space or basement pumps. d. Hillside dewatering. (4) The following naturally occurring discharges are allowed: a. Naturally occurring groundwater seepage via a storm drain b. Non-anthropogenic flows from a naturally occurring stream via a culvert or storm drain, as long as there are no contributions of anthropogenic runoff. (5) Existing storm water discharges into an SWQPA-GP shall be characterized and assessed to determine what effect if any these inputs are having on natural water quality in the State Water Quality Protection Area. Such assessments shall include an evaluation of cumulative impacts as well as impacts stemming from individual discharges. Information to be considered shall include: a. Water quality; b. Flow; c. Watershed pollutant sources; and d. Intertidal and/ or subtidal biological surveys. Within each SWQPA-GP the assessment shall be used to rank these existing discharges into low, medium and high threat impact categories. Cumulative impacts will be ranked similarly as well. (6) An initial analysis shall be performed for pre- and post-storm receiving water\* quality of Table 1 constituents and chronic toxicity.\* If post-storm receiving water\* quality has larger concentrations of constituents relative to pre-storm, and Table 1 instantaneous maximum concentrations for chemical constituents, and daily maximum concentrations for chronic toxicity,\* are exceeded, then receiving water\* shall be re-analyzed along with storm runoff (end of pipe) for the constituents that are exceeded. (7) If undesirable alterations of natural water quality and/or biological communities are identified, control strategies/measures shall be implemented for those dischargers characterized as a high threat or those contributing to higher threat cumulative impacts first. (8) If those strategies fail, additional control strategies/measures will be implemented for dischargers characterized as medium impact dischargers. If these strategies do not result in improvement of water quality, those discharges classified as low threat shall also implement control strategies/measures. (d) Implementation Provisions for New Discharges See Appendix I for definition of terms. 2015 Ocean Plan ## (1) Point Source Wastewater Outfalls No new point source wastewater outfalls shall be established within an SWQPA-GP. ## (2) Seawater\* intakes No new surface water seawater\* intakes shall be established within an SWQPA-GP. This does not apply to subsurface\* intakes where studies are prepared showing there is no predictable entrainment, impingement, or construction-related marine life mortality. ## (3) All Other New Discharges There shall be no increase in nonpoint sources or permitted storm drains directly into an SWQPA-GP. ## 6. Impaired Tributaries to MPAs, SWQPA-ASBS and SWQPA-GP All water bodies draining to, or that are designated as, MPAs and SWQPAs that appear on the State’s CWA section 303(d) list shall be given a high priority to have a TMDL developed and implemented. ## F. 在环境空气质量方面，GB 3095-2012《环境空气质量标准》表1为环境空气基本污染物项目浓度限值表，涵盖二氧化硫、二氧化氮、一氧化碳、臭氧及粒径小于等于10μm和2.5μm的颗粒物等项目，基本项目在全国范围内实施；GB 3095-2026表1列出上述项目的过渡阶段及一级、二级浓度限值。另有表1规定采样点数量最多可减少50%时各污染物最低采样点数量，按区域人口分档，涵盖二氧化氮、二氧化硫、一氧化碳、苯、PM10、PM2.5、PM10中的铅、镉、砷、镍及苯并(a)芘，最低数量从1个到5个不等。欧盟附件VII第1节的表1规定设于城市背景位置的监测超级站点须测量的污染物及测量类型，包括PM10、PM2.5、UFP、BC、NO2、O3、SO2、CO、超细颗粒物粒径分布、苯并(a)芘及其他多环芳烃及其总沉降、砷镉铅镍及其总沉降、苯和PM2.5化学组成。2022年欧洲空气质量状况报告的表1汇总环境空气质量指令为保护健康确立的空气质量标准，其中O3的信息和警报阈值及NO2、SO2的警报阈值未在该报告中分析。

在水质与室内空气方面，GB 5084-2021《农田灌溉水质标准》表1为农田灌溉用水基本控制项目限值表，按水田作物、旱地作物和蔬菜三类分别给出pH、水温、悬浮物、五日生化需氧量、化学需氧量、阴离子表面活性剂、氯化物、硫化物、全盐量、总铅、总镉、铬、总汞、总砷、粪大肠菌群数和蛔虫卵数等限值。GB 18466-2005表1为传染病和结核病医疗机构污水污染物排放标准值表，共26项控制项目，包括粪大肠菌群数、肠道致病菌、肠道病毒、结核杆菌、pH、COD、BOD、SS、氨氮、总余氯、斑马鱼卵急性毒性及总镉、总铬、六价铬、总砷、总铅、总银、总α放射性、总β放射性等；修改单对其第23至25项及表注内容进行修改，并增加第26项控制项目及标准值；其第16～22项在科室处理设施排出口取样。《室内空气质量标准》表1按物理性、化学性、生物性、放射性四个参数类别列出19项参数的序号、单位、标准值及备注，并注明新风量要求不低于标准值，除温度和相对湿度外的其它参数要求不高于标准值。此外，表1还包含为保护市政与工业有益用途而设的水质目标，地表水环境质量标准基本项目标准限值表亦以表1形式呈现。另有表1规定现有制浆造纸企业水污染物排放限值，包含pH值、色度、悬浮物、BOD5、CODCr、氨氮、总氮、总磷、AOX等指标及单位产品基准排水量。还有表1列出受沉积物质量条款保护的有益用途及其对应目标受体，另有表1为规划清单表格，列出在至少80%置信水平下将水体列入规划清单所需的不满足适用水质基准的最低样本数量。此外，存在用于水质变化趋势分析对照的规定表格。另有表1为按有益用途和水体类型列出“C”值（如12 ng/L、4 ng/L、1 ng/L总汞或逐案确定）的数据表，用于确定排放者的合理潜能和排放限值。

在排放方面，锅炉大气污染物排放标准表1按燃煤锅炉、以油为燃料的锅炉或燃气轮机组、以气体为燃料的锅炉或燃气轮机组等类型分别规定污染物项目、适用条件、限值及污染物排放监控位置。GB 28662-2012表1规定现有企业自2012年10月1日至2014年12月31日执行的大气污染物排放限值。在用锅炉相关标准表1规定在用锅炉自2015年10月1日或2016年7月1日起执行的排放限值，按燃煤、燃油、燃气锅炉分别给出颗粒物、二氧化硫、氮氧化物、汞及其化合物和烟气黑度限值。机动车排放标准表1汇总中国现行新生产机动车排放标准，按车辆类型分列标准标号和标准名称，反映截至2020年12月31日的现行标准情况。此外，Table 1还列出化学物质瞬时最大浓度和慢性毒性日最大浓度限值。

在环境影响评价方面，相关标准表1规定建设项目和规划项目SO2、NOx及VOCs的年排放量门槛：建设项目SO2+NOx≥500 t/a对应二次PM2.5；规划项目SO2+NOx≥500 t/a对应二次PM2.5，NOx+VOCs≥2000 t/a对应O3；当污染物年排放量达到表1规定的量时，可按表4推荐的方法预测二次污染物。此外，“表1”亦见于气象数据文献，指展示2024年珠江区降水量与上年和多年平均值比较情况的数据表；2024年水资源一级区降水量统计表也以“表1”形式呈现，包含各一级区降水量及与多年平均值、2023年的比较。另有表1为包含测试物种及相关参数的表格，用于选择测试物种，涉及测试方法选择时的盐度和层级分类。此外，还存在一种断面水质类别与水质定性评价分级对应关系表，以“表1”形式列出水质类别、水质状况、表征颜色和水质功能。含氯消毒剂设计相关表格中，采用含氯消毒剂时按表1、表2要求设计。

## 2 Introduction
The 2022 Status report ofair quality in Europe presents summarized information on the air quality data reported as measurements data under the 2023 September reporting cycle (validated assessment data for 2022, deadline of submission 30 September 2023). This report aims at informing on the 2022 status of ambient air quality in Europe and on progress towards meeting the air quality standards established for the protection of health in the Ambient Air Quality Directives (EU, 2004, 2008) (Table 1) and the World Health Organization air quality guideline levels (WHO, 2000, 2006, 2021) (Table 2)(<sup>4</sup>).
This report builds on the former EEA “Air quality in Europe report” (EEA, 2020) content, figures and maps regarding the status of monitored air quality in Europe. It provides:
• a European overview of the 2022 monitoring stations reported, and of their concentrations in relation to the EU legal standards and WHO AQG levels for each pollutant;
• a map with the 2022 concentrations at station level for each pollutant;
• a boxplot graph summarizing for each country the range of concentrations (highlighting the lowest, highest, average and the 25 and 75 percentiles) for $\mathsf { P M } _ { 1 0 } , \mathsf { P M } _ { 2 . 5 } , \mathsf { N O } _ { 2 } , \mathsf { O } _ { 3 }$ and BaP.
Furthermore, it provides:
• maps with the situation at station level for the previous three years. In this way, any significant change in the spatial distribution of the values above the set thresholds in the legends can be observed;
• heatmaps with the evolution of the mean and the maximum measured concentrations at country level since 2000 (or since when available).

Implementation Provisions for SWQPAs-GP\* (a) Implementation provisions for existing point source wastewater discharges (NPDES) (1) An SWQPA-GP shall not be designated over existing permitted point source wastewater outfalls or encroach upon the zone of initial dilution\* associated with an existing discharge. This requirement does not apply to discharges less than one million gallons per day. (2) Designation of an SWQPA-GP shall not include conditions to move existing point source wastewater outfalls. (3) Where a new SWQPA-GP is established in the vicinity of existing municipal wastewater outfalls, there shall be no new or modified limiting condition or prohibitions for the SWQPA-GP relative to those wastewater outfalls. (4) Regulatory requirements for discharges from existing treated municipal wastewater outfalls shall be derived from the Chapter II – Water Quality Objectives and Chapter III – Program of Implementation. (b) Implementation provisions for existing seawater\* intakes (1) Existing permitted seawater\* intakes other than those serving desalination facilities\* must be controlled to minimize entrainment and impingement by using best technology available. Existing permitted seawater\* intakes with a capacity less than one million gallons per day are excluded from this requirement. (2) Existing permitted seawater\* intakes serving desalination facilities are governed by the provisions set forth in chapter III.M of this Plan. (c) Implementation provisions for permitted separate storm sewer system (MS4) discharges and nonpoint source discharges. (1) Existing waste\* discharges are allowed, but shall not cause an undesirable alteration in natural water quality. For purposes of SWQPA-GP, an undesirable alteration in natural water quality means that for intermittent (e.g. wet weather) discharges, Table 1 instantaneous maximum concentrations for chemical constituents, and daily maximum concentrations for chronic toxicity,\* must not be exceeded in the receiving water.\* (2) An NPDES permitting authority\* may authorize NPDES-permitted non-storm water discharges\* to an MS4 with a direct discharge to an SWQPA-GP only to the extent the NPDES permitting authority\* finds that the discharge does not cause an undesirable alteration in natural water quality in an SWQPA-GP. (3) Non-storm water (dry weather) flows are effectively prohibited as required by the applicable permit. Where capacity and infrastructure exists, all dry weather flows shall be diverted to municipal sanitary sewer systems. The permitting authority\* may allow discharges essential for emergency response purposes, structural stability, and slope stability, which may include but are not limited the following: See Appendix I for definition of terms. 2015 Ocean Plan a. Discharges associated with emergency fire-fighting operations. b. Foundation and footing drains c. Water from crawl space or basement pumps. d. Hillside dewatering. (4) The following naturally occurring discharges are allowed: a. Naturally occurring groundwater seepage via a storm drain b. Non-anthropogenic flows from a naturally occurring stream via a culvert or storm drain, as long as there are no contributions of anthropogenic runoff. (5) Existing storm water discharges into an SWQPA-GP shall be characterized and assessed to determine what effect if any these inputs are having on natural water quality in the State Water Quality Protection Area. Such assessments shall include an evaluation of cumulative impacts as well as impacts stemming from individual discharges. Information to be considered shall include: a. Water quality; b. Flow; c. Watershed pollutant sources; and d. Intertidal and/ or subtidal biological surveys. Within each SWQPA-GP the assessment shall be used to rank these existing discharges into low, medium and high threat impact categories. Cumulative impacts will be ranked similarly as well. (6) An initial analysis shall be performed for pre- and post-storm receiving water\* quality of Table 1 constituents and chronic toxicity.\* If post-storm receiving water\* quality has larger concentrations of constituents relative to pre-storm, and Table 1 instantaneous maximum concentrations for chemical constituents, and daily maximum concentrations for chronic toxicity,\* are exceeded, then receiving water\* shall be re-analyzed along with storm runoff (end of pipe) for the constituents that are exceeded. (7) If undesirable alterations of natural water quality and/or biological communities are identified, control strategies/measures shall be implemented for those dischargers characterized as a high threat or those contributing to higher threat cumulative impacts first. (8) If those strategies fail, additional control strategies/measures will be implemented for dischargers characterized as medium impact dischargers. If these strategies do not result in improvement of water quality, those discharges classified as low threat shall also implement control strategies/measures. (d) Implementation Provisions for New Discharges See Appendix I for definition of terms. 2015 Ocean Plan ## (1) Point Source Wastewater Outfalls No new point source wastewater outfalls shall be established within an SWQPA-GP. ## (2) Seawater\* intakes No new surface water seawater\* intakes shall be established within an SWQPA-GP. This does not apply to subsurface\* intakes where studies are prepared showing there is no predictable entrainment, impingement, or construction-related marine life mortality. ## (3) All Other New Discharges There shall be no increase in nonpoint sources or permitted storm drains directly into an SWQPA-GP. ## 6.
